## Purpose

This notebook explains `_targets.R` as a reproducibility mechanism. The pipeline formalizes dependency tracking between configuration, data transformations, model artifacts, and reporting outputs.

## Setup

```{r}
library(targets)
source("R/core.R")
```

## 1) Pipeline script inspection

```{r}
# Reading the target script is useful for auditing computational lineage.
# In an academic context, this helps demonstrate that outputs are derived from explicit dependencies.
cat(readLines("_targets.R"), sep = "\n")
```

## 2) Why targets matter for research reproducibility

The `targets` framework:

- tracks upstream/downstream dependencies
- re-runs only invalidated steps
- stores computational artifacts for inspection
- improves auditability of empirical results

## 3) Execute pipeline

```{r}
# tar_make() executes only what is outdated.
# This property is critical for reproducible iteration in empirical projects.
tar_make()
```

## 4) Inspect key target artifacts

```{r}
# Extracting target outputs makes post-hoc methodological review straightforward.
# Metrics and predictions are typically the first artifacts examined in model evaluation.
metrics <- tar_read(metrics)
predictions <- tar_read(predictions)

metrics
head(predictions, 10)
```

## 5) Report target behavior

```{r}
# The report target is resilient to missing Quarto CLI.
# If Quarto is unavailable, a sentinel value is produced instead of hard-failing the full pipeline.
tar_read(report)
```

## Notes for extension
